findings.byte_indexing: Saved output mappings are 32 distinct uninverted wires for both modes. All eight initial/feedback address-source permutations, with inversion signs excluded, match byte-local ROR8(input,1). All four ROM-to-output mappings match destination (j+1)%4 and output-bit permutation [0,4,2,6,1,5,3,7].
findings.identity_count: 4096 is correct: four byte slots times 256 byte inputs times four equalities (forward initial=feedback; inverse initial=feedback; inverse after forward=identity; forward after inverse=identity). This is not 4096 whole-word or clocked tests.
findings.inverse_equation: Forward destination (j+1)%4 implies inverse output j = S^-1(input[(j+1)%4]) XOR K[j]. The script uses this indexing correctly.
findings.phase_composition: The separately proven synchronized counters enable RAM/working-state updates on launch-inclusive edges1-4. The edge4 result is held for the edge5 CS-high serial-bank load. Pure four-iteration composition in check_key_handling_structure.py agrees with this schedule; it does not alone prove arbitrary clocked behavior.
findings.key_claim: No runtime key register or transaction claim is scoped to normal-operation reconstruction; fixed literals and disabled RAM writes support that limit. No claim of original mask provenance or arbitrary malformed-protocol behavior is warranted.
findings.standard_name: The normalized-substitution digest can identify the AES S-box using the coordinator independent reference. It does not identify the full 32-bit four-update construction as the standard AES block cipher.
